notes: PMS-survey rule: INCLUDE (reports % with acne worsening premenstrually). PSST stem asks about symptoms that start before the period and stop after bleeding; 40.4% of 285 students report premenstrual 'acne flare-ups'. Borderline and weak: exact acne item wording not given; general student population; some used menstrual-delaying (hormonal) medicine. Full text PMC12302784.

PMS-survey rule: EXCLUDE (acne only a symptom count). PMDD survey (Brazil); acne/skin oiliness prevalence, severity and associations with other symptoms, by age group; nothing compared across cycle phases. Full text PMC12411650. Possibly overlaps the same Brazilian survey programme as PMID:39319606 (both excluded).

PMS-survey rule: EXCLUDE (acne only a symptom count). Adapted PSST, acne/oily skin prevalence and severity by age group in the 15 days before menses; no contrast with another phase. Full text PMC11823361.

PMS-survey rule: EXCLUDE (acne only a symptom count). Students picked 'acne/pimples' from a list of PMS symptoms felt before their last period (39.2%); no worsening framing and no other-phase comparison. Full text PMC7648490.
PMS-survey rule: EXCLUDE (acne only a symptom count). 'Acne/skin blemish' premenstrual symptom severity (62% any); comparisons are by ethnicity and HC use, not by cycle phase. Full text PMC5615478.

PMS-survey rule: INCLUDE (phase comparison). Symptoms, acne among them, rated premenstrual vs preovulatory phase within one cycle in 103 asthmatic women; practically all symptoms increased premenstrually (effect sizes). Need full text to confirm the acne-specific effect size and whether HC users were excluded; indirect population (asthma). Full text not obtained (publisher blocked automated access).
PMS-survey rule: EXCLUDE (acne only a symptom count). Menarche survey; acne listed as a common complaint 'during the menstrual period'; no phase contrast. Full text not obtained.
Women chosen for cyclic/premenstrual dermatoses; compares hormones with controls and reports tamoxifen treatment; skin not compared across phases (drug-treatment rule).

Sanitary pad trial: vulvar TEWL/irritation compared between pad types and a no-pad control period while pads were used for two whole cycles; the contrast is product use, not cycle phase. Genital site. Full text not obtained.
Duplicate report: Agner doctoral thesis summary that re-reports the day 1 vs days 9-11 SLS reactivity result already included as PMID:2033132 (Agner, Damm, Skouby 1991).
Narrative clinical description (Kligman) of post-adolescent acne; says premenstrual flares are 'typical' but gives no data.

No PubMed abstract; publisher abstract found via OpenAlex. Double-blind trial of hydrochlorothiazide vs placebo started 7 days before menses in 21 patients; no effect. Drug-treatment rule: no phase comparison of skin, no phase-timed skincare.

No abstract in PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar; no DOI or online full text (Pa Med J 1960). PubMed keywords (chlorothiazide therapy) suggest it would fall under the drug-treatment rule (NO_PHASE_COMPARISON) anyway.

No formal abstract; basis is the publisher's opening paragraph (via OpenAlex): chlorothiazide given to 20 patients with severe premenstrual flares (1-page report). Drug-treatment rule: no phase comparison, no phase-timed skincare.

Full text (Acta Derm Venereol free archive). Forehead sebum excretion rate weekly x8 in 10 women with mild acne, regular cycles, no OC; fell in 1st half, rose in luteal phase, fell premenstrually.
